notes: todos declares a soft-delete column (D-corpus-soft-delete-and-refusal context grammar): the app marks a row deleted by writing that column, so a hard delete would send a tombstone the table's own model does not admit

the row is inserted first, so the refusal is measured against a LIVE row and a NON-EMPTY outbox: the engine refuses op:'delete' with the local error SOFT_DELETE_VIOLATION before anything is written (P:outbox-and-serial-in-flight: the row and its outbox entry are one transaction, so a refusal leaves neither)

after the refusal the row is still readable and the outbox still holds exactly the insert: a client that hard-deletes fails the local-row check and a client that queues the delete fails the outbox-depth check

title: delete on a soft-delete table: refused locally, nothing queued
